notes.W7154454518: Later-born cohorts both enter old age with better episodic memory and decline more slowly, across ~219,000 people in five cohorts. The size of the effect could plausibly explain the 13% per-decade fall in dementia incidence. Caveat: cohort and period effects are bounded, not fully separated.
notes.W7110625727: A cross-randomised trial in 415 Kenyan villages: an 80-minute aspirations workshop raised labour supply, investment, revenue and living standards 17 months later versus a placebo workshop, and cash transfers raised aspirations too. Psychology and economics act through one shared mechanism here.
notes.W4406810358: Reframes the cause of Mediterranean sapropels: not Nile floods, but less net evaporation because atmospheric rivers shifted south during negative Arctic Oscillation phases at insolation maxima. A water-budget switch in the atmosphere collapses deep overturning and brings anoxia.
notes.W7156713044: Solves a chaotic random recurrent network for one fixed weight matrix, with no averaging over synapses, giving the first 1/N correction to correlations and responses. That links a specific connectome to its spontaneous activity and perturbation response, and proves the Shen–Hu conjecture.
notes.W7236707489: Aerosols from 21 cruises constrain a global model: organic nitrogen supplies ~27% of nitrogen deposited on oceans (12.8 Tg N per year), and ~50% in nitrogen-limited seas. A long-ignored nutrient term in ocean biogeochemistry. Uncertainty bands remain wide (11–40%).
notes.W4415065700: A learning task, predicting Tr[f(H)ρ] for an unknown function f, that is provably easy for quantum computers and hard classically. It uses Fourier features of Hamiltonians plus linear regression and runs on 72 superconducting qubits. Quantum advantage on a physically meaningful task.
notes.W7236565982: Argues amyloid cross-seeding is directional: A seeding B tells you little about B seeding A. Sets out six mechanisms behind the asymmetry and warns that bulk aggregation assays can't tell templated growth from secondary nucleation. Relevant to mixed proteinopathies such as Alzheimer's with Lewy pathology.
notes.W7128466625: A 1.29-gram flapping-wing robot hovers and tracks trajectories using only onboard IMU, optical flow, time-of-flight sensing and a microcontroller, reaching centimetre accuracy outside motion capture. Insect-scale flight leaves the lab. Caveat: power is still tethered and the demo flight lasted 30 seconds.
notes.W4417450774: Opposition to dense housing is partly a sociotropic aesthetic judgement about whether buildings 'fit', not only homeowner self-interest. Experiments show that dislike of tall buildings causally lowers support. Points to design and siting, not just compensation, as policy levers.
notes.W4415345631: Proves that any bounded sequence of matrices, perturbed by small absolutely continuous noise, gives a product whose log singular values separate by at least about ε²n. A quantitative, non-stationary guarantee that noise breaks degeneracy, relevant to the stability of numerical and physical simulations.

thread: Two Earth-system picks find the atmosphere doing work that had been credited elsewhere. Mediterranean anoxia follows from atmospheric rivers changing the sea's net evaporation, not from river floods. Organic nitrogen carried through the air supplies about half of the nitrogen deposited in nitrogen-starved seas. In both cases the missing term in an ocean budget was moisture or matter moving through the sky.

notes.W7236305771: Shifts: interstitial oxygen in metals is randomly distributed → it occupies correlated sites, forming nanoscale ordered domains along [0001], seen directly by 3D ptychography. Models of strengthening, transport and phase stability built on random-solution assumptions need revisiting.
notes.W4416048293: Shifts: the 1957 Huang–Yang energy expansion for dilute repulsive fermions was a physicist's prediction → a theorem, with matching upper and lower bounds. It confirms rigorously that low-density Fermi gas energetics depend only on the scattering length, to third order.
notes.W4411174673: Shifts: genotype–phenotype maps are fixed backdrops on which selection acts → the maps themselves evolve to maximise the number of genotypes that give fit phenotypes. This yields 'frequency matching' in regulatory architecture and a candidate mathematical definition of evolvability.
notes.W7160248457: Shifts: efficient tissue tiling and large-scale order are separate properties needing separate controls → one local rule, growth coupled to neighbour repulsion, produces both and drives tissues to hyperuniformity. Confirmed in retinal microglia. Global order emerges from purely local interaction.

foundation.title: One typical instance carries the ensemble's laws
foundation.principle: In large random systems, quantities like Lyapunov exponents, singular-value gaps and correlation functions self-average: a single typical realisation obeys the same laws as the ensemble, with corrections that can be computed. The chaotic network paper uses this at fixed connectivity. It no longer averages over weights but obtains the 1/N correction tied to the specific matrix, so the gap between quenched and annealed behaviour becomes something you can calculate. The Inventiones paper gives the dynamical counterpart: a fixed, non-stationary sequence of matrices plus minimal noise already has well-separated exponents, so typical behaviour is forced by noise rather than assumed. The same logic underlies spin glasses, the spectra of disordered media, and why one long simulation run can stand in for many.
rests_on: Furstenberg & Kesten (1960). Products of random matrices
Sompolinsky, Crisanti & Sommers (1988). Chaos in random neural networks
foundation.question: How large must a specific network or matrix sequence be before its own structure, rather than ensemble statistics, dominates its dynamics, and can we predict that crossover from the connectivity alone?

W7154454518.question: Is falling dementia incidence due to higher cognition entering old age, slower decline, or both?
W7154454518.approach: ~783,000 episodic memory assessments from ~219,000 people across five longitudinal cohorts, plus hippocampal atrophy data and bounding analysis.
W7154454518.finding: Later cohorts have higher memory and slower decline; the 20-year cohort advantage at 80 could explain a 13% per-decade incidence fall.
W7154454518.implication: Cognitive ageing is malleable through lifespan environment; dementia risk is shifting across generations, not fixed.

W7110625727.question: Do higher aspirations drive long-term investment among people in poverty, and do aspirations respond to economic gains?
W7110625727.approach: 415-village field experiment, 8,300 Kenyan women; aspirations workshop cross-randomised with large unconditional cash transfers.
W7110625727.finding: Workshop raised aspirations, labour supply, investment, revenue and living standards at 17 months; cash transfers also raised aspirations.
W7110625727.implication: Aspirations are a causal lever in development policy, movable by both psychological and economic interventions.

W4406810358.question: What caused abrupt Mediterranean freshening, circulation collapse and anoxic sapropels at insolation maxima?
W4406810358.approach: Compared western Mediterranean surface-salinity records with Atlantic Iberian Margin winter precipitation records.
W4406810358.finding: Low-salinity events coincided with heavy Iberian rain, from equatorward atmospheric-river shifts during negative Arctic Oscillation phases.
W4406810358.implication: Atmospheric moisture balance, not only Nile runoff, controls Mediterranean ventilation; a lens for future circulation change.

W7156713044.question: Can a chaotic random recurrent network be solved for one fixed weight matrix rather than averaged over weights?
W7156713044.approach: Diagrammatic large-N technique computing moments and response functions without synaptic averaging.
W7156713044.finding: Obtained the first nontrivial 1/N term for intensive correlation functions, proving the Shen–Hu conjecture as a special case.
W7156713044.implication: Analytically links a specific connectivity to spontaneous correlations and perturbation responses.

W7236707489.question: How much organic nitrogen does the atmosphere deposit into the global ocean?
W7236707489.approach: Marine aerosol measurements from 21 cruises used to constrain and evaluate an updated atmospheric chemistry model.
W7236707489.finding: 12.8 (4.0–22.7) Tg N/yr, 27% of total N deposition; 70% terrestrial sources; ~50% in N-limited regions.
W7236707489.implication: Ocean nutrient budgets and productivity models must include atmospheric organic nitrogen.

W4415065700.question: Is there a practically meaningful learning task provably easy quantumly and hard classically?
W4415065700.approach: Predict Tr[f(H)ρ] using Hamiltonian Fourier feature maps with linear regression; experiment on superconducting hardware.
W4415065700.finding: Learnability proven theoretically and demonstrated on a device with up to 72 qubits.
W4415065700.implication: A near-term-feasible quantum advantage tied to physically relevant quantities.

W7236565982.question: Why does amyloid cross-seeding often work in one direction but not the reverse?
W7236565982.approach: Review integrating kinetic, structural, cellular, animal and human evidence, plus simulation and machine-learning approaches.
W7236565982.finding: Proposes directional compatibility, with six mechanisms; bulk assays cannot separate elongation from secondary nucleation or sequestration.
W7236565982.implication: A framework for mixed amyloid pathologies and for blocking or redirecting heterotypic propagation.

W7128466625.question: Can an insect-scale aerial robot fly stably with only onboard sensing and computation?
W7128466625.approach: 1.29 g flapping-wing robot with IMU, optical flow, time-of-flight sensor, MCU, estimators and hierarchical controller.
W7128466625.finding: Centimetre-scale positional accuracy; 30-second flight outside motion capture avoiding obstacles and landing on a sunflower.
W7128466625.implication: Moves microrobots toward field use; onboard planning and power autonomy are next.

W4417450774.question: Beyond self-interest and NIMBYism, what drives opposition to dense housing?
W4417450774.approach: Theory of sociotropic aesthetic judgement tested with descriptive studies and experiments.
W4417450774.finding: Density tastes predict support; development is favoured where it 'fits'; aesthetic distaste for tall buildings causally reduces support.
W4417450774.implication: Housing policy can work through design and siting, not only compensating homeowners.

W4415345631.question: How far apart are singular values of non-stationary random matrix products under small noise?
W4415345631.approach: Quantitative, fibered extension of Gorodetski–Kleptsyn relative-entropy methods on flag bundles.
W4415345631.finding: Gaps between log singular values are at least order ε²n, in expectation and almost surely for large n.
W4415345631.implication: Universal guarantee that noise separates all Lyapunov exponents, even without stationarity.

figure_notes.W7154454518: Each line is a birth cohort's episodic memory plotted against age over overlapping age ranges. Read vertically to compare cohorts at the same age: later-born lines sit higher. Read along each line for the slope: later cohorts also decline less steeply. Together these make up the 'double dividend'.
figure_notes.W4406810358: The map shows the Mediterranean basin and the paths of atmospheric rivers reaching southern Europe. Notice the Atlantic Iberian Margin as the main moisture gateway. When those river paths shift south, more Atlantic moisture enters the basin, net evaporation falls and surface water freshens. That is the paper's trigger for sapropels.
figure_notes.W7156713044: This is the paper's diagram key: the graphical symbols for propagators, vertices and connectivity used in the 1/N expansion. Learn it first. Each later correlation or response function is a sum of these diagrams, and their structure shows how a fixed weight matrix enters without averaging.
figure_notes.W7128466625: Panel A shows the payoff, a landing on a sunflower. B–E show the robot before and after fitting three tiny boards (IMU, microcontroller, optical flow plus time-of-flight). F explains how this is possible: a scaled-up module gives 46% more lift to carry the sensors. G is a composite of obstacle-avoiding flight outside motion capture.
